finding.text: There is no `requirements.md` in the task folder, so the owner's ask exists only as the truncated `assign.title` in `session.jsonl:1`, and there is no outcome or landing line. A fresh agent cannot tell from this folder what was asked or whether it is done. Write the brief, quoting the owner's 2026-10-26 words, and land the task: branch `worktree/tasks-stay-in-session` (6e6dd094d, cb6213d44) is still unmerged.

`public/framework/ai/doc/tasks.md:281` (diff) says "a module's page finds its tasks through the index (`AIIndex` rows carry `module`)". That is false for the new default. `Server/AIIndex.mjs:73-79` (`kind`) indexes only record files, so a task nested as a line in `session.jsonl` gets no row and no `module`. The agent's own log in `session.jsonl` says the same ("Index covers module tasks … but not tasks nested in session.jsonl"). As it stands, every newly filed task disappears from module pages and from `/framework/ai/tasks/`. Either index nested tasks with their `module` tag, or stop the doc from promising it.

`public/framework/ai/tasks/readme.md:9,21` still describes the module folder as where "a task that belongs to a module" lives, and still says the item tool's `tasks.add` makes "a module task". Both are stale now, and the readme leaves out the new rule and `Server/TaskToSession.mjs`. `ai/doc/tasks.md` changed, but this index page did not.

`move_to_session` (`page_tools.js`, diff lines 179-199) does git moves and appends to the ledger, and nothing tests it. `item_tool.test.mjs` and `prompt-tasks.test.mjs` both pass (106 and 23 checks), but neither calls it. It also skips `record_new_folder`, which `move_home` calls, so the moved folder never reaches the session folder's `files.jsonl` index (law 10). Add a scratch-dir test and the index call.

The new test "module is a tag, not a home" (`item_tool.test.mjs`, diff line 101-102) checks for the folder `module-from-path`, but the task it files is titled "Module tag only". The assertion passes no matter what that call does; it should check `module-tag-only`.

The new add key `home` reuses a name that already means something else. A top-level `{"home": "<url>"}` line is TaskMigrate's alias (`Server/AIIndex.mjs:134,196`, `TaskMigrate.mjs:202`), and it replays as `data.home`. If an add names a module that has no folder (`home: "nomod"`), the task nests, keeps `home: "nomod"` in its data, and quietly gets no module folder. Consider another key name (for example `module_home`), or refuse the add when the module folder doesn't exist.
It is simpler and correct to switch off `PromptTasks.MODULE_HOMES` with a static flag instead of deleting the sweep. `core/Session/doc/prompt-tasks.md` item 7 now says so up front.

`move_home` is broken: the fix for the earlier review put `await record_new_folder(sdir, slug);` in the wrong function (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:581`, diff line 272). `sdir` doesn't exist in `move_home`, so it throws a ReferenceError after the git mv, the line writes and the ledger line have already happened. `node Servex/ProcessRunner.test.mjs` fails on the branch ("it records its new path and the run goes on there") and passes on michael/dev (43 passing). In production, `ProcessRunner.js:77` catches the error as `home_refused` even though the folder has already moved. Move that line to the end of `move_to_session`, before its `return`.

`move_to_session` still never calls `record_new_folder`, so a moved folder never reaches the session folder's `files.jsonl` (law 10). The earlier review's finding 4 is only half done: the test exists now, but the index call landed in `move_home` instead (see 1).

Deliverable 5 is not done. `ai/sessions/2026/10/25/v-9dvbbrn/` holds only `session.jsonl` and `ai/`, and the brief does not name the four module tasks to move. Name them in `requirements.md` (or a `moves.md`), with the exact `node Server/TaskToSession.mjs … --go` line, so a fresh agent can finish the move after the merge. The branch `worktree/tasks-stay-in-session` (369a69bea) is still unmerged, and the task has no landing line.

`ai/doc/tasks.md` (diff line 379) says "a module's page finds its tasks through the index (`open_nested` … with its `module` tag)". Nothing in `public/` reads `open_nested` yet (grep finds no reader), so a module page does not show session-filed tasks today. Either say "can find", or file the module-page reader as a follow-up task.

The add key `home` still clashes with TaskMigrate's `{"home":"<url>"}` alias line (`Server/AIIndex.mjs` `alias`, earlier review's finding 6). An add with `home: "nomod"`, where that module has no folder, nests quietly and keeps `home` in its data. The new test only checks the folder path ("the home key is not stored as data"). Refusing an unknown `home`, or stripping it on the nest path, would close this.

Simpler, and correct: the steering fix is small. It is one key in `task_home`, a `MODULE_HOMES` flag and text in the rules and docs. Every doc listed in deliverable 2 is updated, and the two superseded owner notes now carry a pointer banner.

While reviewing, I mistakenly ran `git stash` in the main checkout. I put every change back by hand (131 files from the stash diff, plus `v-9dvbbrn/session.jsonl` merged in order: the stashed lines, then the newer ones). Today's working tree now equals the stash plus the newer appends. The stash entry `df7a8da3d` is still in the stash list, because the git guard blocks `git stash drop`. It is redundant and can be dropped.
